questions.question: What is namespacing in Ruby and why use it?
questions.title: Namespacing in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Namespacing groups related classes/modules under a module to avoid name collisions and organize code. `module Payments; class Charge; end; class Refund; end; end` -> Payments::Charge, Payments::Refund. The `::` is the scope resolution operator. Without namespacing, two Charge classes would clash; with it, Payments::Charge and Orders::Charge coexist. Constants are resolved via :: (Math::PI). Modules also namespace methods (module-level methods called as M.method or via extend/include). Rails uses namespacing heavily (Admin::UsersController, API::V1::SessionsController). Benefits: prevents collisions (especially in gems), organizes large codebases, clarifies intent (Payments::Charge is obviously a payment charge). Put related things in a module; reference them with ::. Convention: module names CamelCase, one module per conceptual area.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know namespacing uses modules + :: to group classes and avoid name collisions.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Forgetting the :: (writing Charge inside module Payments but referencing it as Charge, not Payments::Charge), or over-nesting.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Namespacing = modules + :: to group related classes (Payments::Charge), avoid collisions, organize code. Rails uses it (Admin::UsersController).

flowchart LR
  M[module Payments] --> C[Payments::Charge]

sections.title: Namespacing
sections.content:
```ruby
# Namespace related classes under a module
module Payments
  class Charge
    def call; 'charging'; end
  end
  class Refund
    def call; 'refunding'; end
  end
end

# Reference with :: (scope resolution)
Payments::Charge.new.call   # 'charging'
Payments::Refund.new.call   # 'refunding'

# NO collision: a different Charge can coexist
module Orders
  class Charge
    def call; 'order charge'; end
  end
end
Orders::Charge.new.call     # 'order charge'
Payments::Charge.new.call   # 'charging'  (different class)

# Constants via ::
Math::PI                   # 3.14159...
File::SEPARATOR           # '/'

# Nested namespaces (common in Rails):
module API
  module V1
    class SessionsController; end
  end
end
API::V1::SessionsController

# Module-level methods (called as M.method):
module Math2
  def self.square(x); x * x; end
end
Math2.square(3)           # 9

# Benefits: prevent collisions (gems), organize, clarify intent.
# Convention: CamelCase module names, one module per area.
```
